Thus, the appellant is exempted from effecting service on respondent No.1.

The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 29.4.2022 passed in MACC No.111/2021 challenging quantum of compensation on the ground of incorrect assessment of income of the deceased.
The liability of the Insurance Company for death due to accident by the insrued vehicle is not under dispute.
2. Short facts of the case are that deceased Khalil Khan was employed as Driver of Truck No.MP-09-GE-8964.
On 17.9.2020 he was transporting the goods to Sendhwa by the said truck.

When the truck reached near Jamnya NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24930 2 MA-3685-2022 Taper (speed breaker), Truck No.RJ-05-GB-5072 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and without giving any horn dashed into the truck of deceased.
Because of which the Truck of Khalil upturned resulting in grievous injuries to him, because of which he died.
2.1 The claimants-appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for death of Khalil.

The claims Tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded compensation of Rs.14,23,000/- for loss of of dependency and after awarding further amount of Rs.2,70,000/- in other heads total compensation of Rs.16,93,000/- was awarded to the appellants.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims Tribunal after considering the evidence as rendered by Afreen Bi (AW-2) and Ex.P/21, which was salary certificate of deceased Afreen Bee Khan vs Arif Khan on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125786772/

sentences.text: His contention is that once the fact of deceased being Driver was accepted by the claims Tribunal, then his income at Rs.15,000/- could not have been discarded.
He further submits that after discarding claim of income the Tribunal went on to take the income of the deceased at Rs.7,057/- by treating him semi-skilled labour.
However, at the relevant time i.e. on 17.9.2020 as per the guidelines issued by State Legal Services Authority minimum wages for semi-skilled labour were Rs.9,257/- per month.
Thus, even on this count the claims Tribunal was not correct in assessing income of the deceased.

Hence, he prays for enhancement of compensation by quantifying the same based on correct income of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:24930 3 MA-3685-2022 deceased.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the claims Tribunal considered the salary certificate Ex.P/21 and after recording the fact that the employer of the deceased was available in Sendhwa itself, however, he was not brought for examination before the claims Tribunal to prove the said salary certificate, discarded the same.
hence, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased.
There was no material to establish income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- per month, neither any bank statement was produced nor any register of payment was brought on record.
he, thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.

6. On perusal of salary certificate Ex.P/21, though it can be seen that it has been issued by employer Anil Agrawal, however, there is no other material to establish income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-
per month.

Looking to the fact that employer was available, still he was not brought before the Tribunal, in the considered view of this Court, the conclusion of the Tribunal is not required to be interfered with regarding disbelieving claim of income of the deceased.
However, on perusal of the guidelines of the State Legal Services Authority it can be seen that income of the semi-skilled labour on the date of accident were Rs.9,257/-.

As such, income of the deceased is taken at such amount and consequently on applying all other factors in terms of the award the compensation for loss of dependency would change to Rs.18,66,096 and total compensation would come to Rs.21,36,096/-.

After deducting the already awarded amount of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24930 4 MA-3685-2022 Rs.16,93,000/- the appellants are now entitled for payment of Rs.4,43,096/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing claim application before the claims Tribunal till its payment.

7. It is seen from the record that the appellants have valued this appeal at Rs.50,000/-, thus the appellants are required to pay deficit Court fees within four weeks from today.
8.
With the aforesaid, the present Misc.Appeal stands disposed off.
